miniProject.title: Two tag-hidden schedules with witnesses and a repaired recurrence
miniProject.brief: Derive two scheduling dynamic programs from blank files, each returning a witness for an independent checker. A differential harness shrinks, pins and repairs one subtly wrong recurrence, training the formulation judgment the capstone needs.
steps: Solve LC 983 Minimum Cost For Tickets with tags hidden: write the subproblem specification, recurrence, base case and evaluation order before code. Return the cost with a witness of the passes bought.

Build the harness: Hypothesis generates small inputs and compares memoized, tabulated and brute-force answers, while a checker validates that each witness covers every travel day at exactly the reported total.
Plant an off-by-one in the pass coverage, let Hypothesis shrink a failure, pin it with `@example` and repair the recurrence. Map the shrunk input to the exact claim the planted recurrence made.

Solve LC 1335 Minimum Difficulty of a Job Schedule with tags hidden, with a state over the first unscheduled job and days left that returns its cut points as a witness. Differential-test against brute force over all cut positions on small inputs.
Prove both recurrences by induction: name the case split, why the state is sufficient, and why no invalid schedule is admitted.
Write a transfer note for each problem: the smallest sufficient state and one smaller state that fails, with a counterexample.
deliverables: Both solutions with specifications, witnesses and an independent witness checker.
The Hypothesis harness with the pinned failure, the planted recurrence and its repair.
The proofs and transfer notes for both problems.
